flashcards.q: What's the defining property that makes a set of goroutines a 'worker pool' rather than unbounded fan-out?
flashcards.a: A fixed, bounded number of goroutines reading from a bounded input channel, which provides real backpressure by blocking the producer once workers are saturated -- versus spawning one goroutine per item with no cap, which grows without limit under a traffic spike.

flashcards.q: How does gRPC propagate deadlines across a service call automatically?
flashcards.a: A client's context.WithTimeout/WithDeadline is serialized into the RPC's HTTP/2 metadata as a grpc-timeout header; the server-side library deserializes it into a real context.Context deadline on receipt -- no application-level convention needed, works identically across languages.

flashcards.q: Why can a gRPC service with multiple healthy backend pods still see wildly uneven traffic distribution?
flashcards.a: gRPC multiplexes many RPCs over ONE long-lived HTTP/2 TCP connection. An L4 (connection-level) load balancer routes once, when the connection is established -- every subsequent RPC on it goes to the same backend, pinning a client's entire traffic to one pod.

flashcards.q: What are the two real fixes for the gRPC connection-pinning load-balancing trap?
flashcards.a: Client-side RPC-level load balancing (gRPC's round_robin service config resolving multiple backend addresses), or an L7-aware proxy (Envoy) that balances individual HTTP/2 streams rather than whole connections.

flashcards.q: Name the three main HNSW parameters and what each controls.
flashcards.a: M = max neighbor connections per node (graph connectivity, fixed at build, drives memory/build cost, 12-48 typical). efConstruction = build-time search breadth (higher = better graph, much slower build, fixed once built). efSearch = query-time search breadth, the ONLY one tunable live per-request, trades recall for latency.

flashcards.q: If vector search recall drops after a re-index and raising efSearch doesn't fully fix it, what should you check?
flashcards.a: efConstruction -- it may have been reduced, producing a lower-quality graph at build time. No amount of query-time efSearch tuning can fully compensate for a structurally worse graph built with a low efConstruction.

flashcards.q: When is building a custom Go vector-search microservice the right call over using a managed vector database?
flashcards.a: Only after profiling proves the managed DB's network hop and abstraction overhead is the actual bottleneck against a genuinely tight latency budget (e.g. sub-10ms p99), or when per-traffic-class efSearch control the managed API doesn't expose is genuinely needed -- not as a default choice.

flashcards.q: What does errgroup.WithContext provide over a hand-rolled sync.WaitGroup plus manual error channel?
flashcards.a: A derived context automatically canceled the moment any goroutine returns a non-nil error (so siblings get a ctx.Done() signal to exit cleanly), and Wait() returns the first error while guaranteeing all goroutines have finished -- coordination that's otherwise hand-wired and error-prone.

flashcards.q: How should you size a CPU-bound worker pool vs an I/O-bound one?
flashcards.a: CPU-bound: cap near GOMAXPROCS -- more workers than logical CPUs adds scheduling overhead with no throughput gain. I/O-bound: size via Little's Law (concurrency ~ downstream throughput x latency) against the downstream's actual capacity, not core count.

flashcards.q: Why isn't gRPC generally the default choice for public/browser-facing APIs despite its wire-level efficiency advantages?
flashcards.a: Browsers can't natively speak gRPC's HTTP/2-trailers-based framing without a proxy translation layer (grpc-web), and REST/JSON's tooling ubiquity, human-readability, and standard HTTP caching semantics matter more for external, partner-facing, debugging-heavy contexts than raw binary efficiency.
